title: False Friend Funeral (Cognate Casualties)
style: funky comedy samba, 115 BPM, brass stabs, theatrical narrator vocal, tambourim, surdo bass drum, agogo bells, cuica, mock-funeral organ intro, gospel choir backing, EN/ES/PT codeswitch, big band horn section, comedic timing, hooky chorus
lyrics:
[Intro — funeral organ, then BREAK to samba]
We are gathered here today
to bury a misunderstanding
with brass and tambourim
let the false friends rest in peace
[organ vamps out, samba kicks in]

[Verse 1 — theatrical narrator]
"Embarazada" sounds like embarrassed, doesn't it?
But in Spanish it means PREGNANT, that's the trick
I told my Madrid boss "estoy muy embarazada"
Now HR is pregnant with questions, ay caramba!

[Pre-Chorus — call and response]
False friends will betray you
mid-sentence they'll fade you
amigos falsos, que pena
amigos falsos, fora!

[Chorus — three languages stacked, brass stabs]
False friends, false friends, bury them deep (EN)
Amigos falsos, los vamos a quemar (ES)
Amigos falsos, não confie não (PT)
One word can end your whole career-eer-eer!

[Verse 2 — rapid-fire]
"Actual" en español means "current," not actual
"Carpeta" is a folder, not the rug under your shoe
"Library" is NOT librería — that's a bookstore, bro
"Pretender" means "to claim" — Spanish doesn't pretend, no!

[Verse 3 — Portuguese twist]
"Puxe" looks like "push" but the door says PULL
"Esquisito" sounds exquisite — it means WEIRD, you fool
"Constipado" — Spanish has a cold, Portuguese has a blockage
Same word, different bodies, different language baggage

[Bridge — slow theatrical, choral]
Rest in peace, dear false friends
We knew you well, we knew you wrong
You ended marriages, ended careers
You ended songs, you ended songs

[Final Chorus — full brass freakout]
False friends, false friends, bury them deep (EN)
Amigos falsos, los vamos a quemar (ES)
Amigos falsos, não confie não (PT)
One word can end your whole career-eer-eer!

[Outro — whispered]
Adios. Tchau. Amen.
